subject: Status notification: Elevated generation retry rate & soft fallbacks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Robert Green <robert.green@bulwark.ai>
Cc: support@bulwark.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Status notification: Elevated generation retry rate & soft fallbacks

Hi Robert —

Quick note to let you know we’re seeing an elevated generation retry rate for some requests from Bulwark AI this morning. The symptom: an increase in automatic retries and more frequent soft fallbacks to our lower-capacity model variant, which can cause longer response tails and occasional truncated outputs. We observed the behavior starting ~08:40 PT and it affected about 3% of Bulwark traffic at peak.

What we’re doing now:
- On-call has opened an incident (JIRA-INC-9281) and is throttling prefetch work to reduce amplification.
- We’ve temporarily disabled a recently deployed routing tweak that increases prefetch fanout for mixed-model requests.
- We’re monitoring token-level latency and retry-loop counters and will revert any changes only after stability is confirmed.

Immediate customer impact:
- Increased P50/P95 generation latency for a subset of multi-model calls.
- Some requests experienced truncated outputs when the fallback model returned shorter generations.

Next updates: I’ll send a follow-up by 11:30 PT with more detail; if we contain it earlier I’ll update you sooner. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your user flows.

—Marissa

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Robert Green <robert.green@bulwark.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Status notification: Elevated generation retry rate & soft fallbacks

Hi all — internal update from on-call and runtime teams:

Root cause (initial): a routing change rolled out last night increased prefetch fanout for requests that include a heavy prompt + retrieval prewarm. In a small percentage of flows this doubled the prefetch path and caused duplicate in-flight requests against the serving pool. The serving runtime’s retry heuristic then interpreted the duplicate response timing as transient failures for some requests, triggering retry logic and fallbacks to the smaller model variant.

Mitigation taken so far:
- Reverted the fanout change (rolled back at 09:02 PT).
- Rate-limited prefetchers for affected customer buckets (including Bulwark) to avoid amplification while we observe.
- Applied a temporary runtime stop-gap that deduplicates prefetch keys at the routing layer.

Impact:
- Peak affected traffic for Bulwark ~3% of requests between 08:40–09:05 PT.
- P95 latency for those flows rose by ~1.8x; generated tokens were frequently shorter during fallback.

Suggested customer-side mitigations if you see headroom issues:
- Temporarily reduce concurrent request windows for batch jobs.
- If you have a pinned model variant for critical flows, route those calls to the pinned variant while we complete the patch.

We expect to monitor for the next 4–6 hours and will provide a postmortem with timeline and permanent fixes.

—Sean
Engineering Lead, Runtime | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Subject: Incident follow-up: containment, next steps, and postmortem link

Hi Robert —

Follow-up after today’s containment steps. Short summary: the fanout change introduced a prefetch duplication path that probabilistically triggered retry/fallback behavior in the runtime. We reverted the change during the incident window; the temporary dedupe at the routing layer plus prefetch rate-limits removed the retry amplification and stabilized response patterns.

What we did today:
- Reverted routing tweak (09:02 PT).
- Applied routing-layer dedupe and prefetch rate-limits (09:08 PT).
- Monitored tokens, retry counters, and fallback rates until normalized (~12:30 PT).

Customer impact for Bulwark AI:
- Affected window: 08:40–12:30 PT.
- Approx. 2.4% of requests observed transient retry loops at peak, with higher P95 latency and occasional truncated outputs on fallback flows.

Planned permanent fixes and timeline:
- Runtime patch to make retry heuristics resilient to duplicate prefetch events (target: 2026-10-25).
- Improve pre-deploy integration tests for fanout/routing changes (ingest filtering added to rollout checklist).
- Postmortem doc (internal + customer copy) available here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB2cPostmortemDraft — we’ll publish the customer-facing postmortem to the status page and follow up with an official RCA by next Wednesday.

Credits / remediation: We know this impacted your production SLAs for a portion of the day. Our account team will reach out separately with a credit proposal aligned to your committed tier — expect that before end of week.

If you’d like an interactive walk-through with our runtime engineers, we can set a short call tomorrow morning PT. Thanks again for your patience and for flagging the timeouts — that helped speed containment.

Best,
—Marissa
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
